dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1301.text: The appearance of visible teeth. Formed from 齒, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1302.text: 𪘧 means to bite, 齚. Formed from 齒, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1303.text: The sound of teeth splitting bone. Formed from 齒, with 𠛱 indicating the sound. Read like 剌.

shuowen:1304.text: To gnaw bone. Formed from 齒, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1305.text: Uneven teeth. Formed from 齒, with 屑 indicating the sound. Read like 切.

shuowen:1306.text: The sound of hard teeth. Formed from 齒, with 吉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1307.text: Unevenly arranged or projecting teeth. Formed from 齒, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1308.text: To bring food back up and chew it. Formed from 齒, with 台 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “For cattle this is called 齝.”

shuowen:1309.text: To bite. Formed from 齒, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1310.text: The appearance of visible teeth. Formed from 齒, with 䏈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1311.text: To bite. Formed from 齒, with 㓞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1312.text: Teeth hurt by sourness. Formed from 齒, with 所 indicating the sound. Read like 楚.

shuowen:1313.text: An old person's teeth, resembling a mortar. Another explanation: a horse's teeth at eight years become mortar-like. Formed from 齒 and 臼; 臼 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1314.text: Teeth that do not meet. Formed from 齒, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1315.text: A sheep's cud. Formed from 齒, with 丗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1316.text: The cud of deer. Formed from 齒, with 益 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1317.text: Hard teeth. Formed from 齒, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1318.text: The sound of gnawing bone. Formed from 齒 and 骨; 骨 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1319.text: The sound of chewing. Formed from 齒, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1320.text: To chew something hard. Formed from 齒, with abbreviated 博 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1321.text: Years of age. Formed from 齒, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1322.text: Large back teeth (molars). The graph is said to depict upper and lower teeth interlocking. All characters in the 牙 category are formed from 牙. [Duan argues that received 牡齒 is a corruption of 壯齒, “large/strong teeth,” not a reference to male teeth.]

shuowen:1323.text: A projecting canine tooth, or a fang conspicuously standing out. Formed from 牙 and 奇; 奇 also indicates the sound. [Duan argues received 武牙 originally read 虎牙.]

shuowen:1324.text: Tooth decay. Formed from 牙, with 禹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1325.text: A person's foot, situated below. Formed from 止 and 口. All characters in the 足 category are formed from 足.

shuowen:1326.text: A foot or hoof. Formed from 足, with 虒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1327.text: The heel of the foot. Formed from 足, with 𥃩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1328.text: The ankle. Formed from 足, with 果 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1329.text: The underside of the foot. Formed from 足, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1330.text: One foot. Formed from 足, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1331.text: To bow in worship. Formed from 足, with 危 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1332.text: To kneel upright. Formed from 足, with 忌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1333.text: To travel smoothly and easily. Formed from 足, with 叔 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Smooth and easy is the Zhou road.”

shuowen:1334.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 足, with 瞿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1335.text: To walk with long shins or extended legs. Formed from 足, with 㫺 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the cautious gait 踧踖.

shuowen:1336.text: The appearance of walking alone and apart. Formed from 足, with 禹 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Walking alone, solitary.”

shuowen:1337.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 足, with 將 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Pipes and stone chimes sound 蹡蹡.”

shuowen:1338.text: A place trodden upon. Formed from 足, with abbreviated 斷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1339.text: The appearance of hastening across. Formed from 足, with 卜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1340.text: To cross. Formed from 足, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1341.text: Light or nimble. Formed from 足, with 戉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1342.text: To raise the feet high when walking. Formed from 足, with 喬 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The young men are high-stepping.”

shuowen:1343.text: Swift; long. Formed from 足, with 攸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1344.text: To move. Formed from 足, with 倉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1345.text: To jump. Formed from 足, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1346.text: To ascend. Formed from 足, with 齊 indicating the sound. The Book of Shang says: “I fall and rise.”

shuowen:1347.text: Swift. Formed from 足, with 翟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1348.text: To kick or tread. Another explanation: to crouch low and curl up. Formed from 足, with 全 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1349.text: To tread upon. Formed from 足, with 就 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1350.text: To tread. Formed from 足, with 聶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1351.text: To cross. Formed from 足, with 夸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1352.text: To trample. Formed from 足, with 𦐇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1353.text: To tread. Formed from 足, with 步 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1354.text: To tread. Formed from 足, with 舀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1355.text: To tread. Formed from 足, with 廛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1356.text: To step upon. Formed from 足, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1357.text: To follow. Formed from 足, with 重 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the appearance of coming and going.

shuowen:1358.text: To kick. Formed from 足, with 㔬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1359.text: To kick. Formed from 足, with 帶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1360.text: To kick. Formed from 足, with 敝 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to limp.

shuowen:1361.text: To stamp or tread with the foot; to give a small kick. Formed from 足, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1362.text: To guard. Formed from 足, with 衞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1363.text: To tread or step, especially in the historical expression for wading through blood that stains the feet. Formed from 足, with 執 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1364.text: To stand upright. Formed from 足, with 氏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1365.text: To plant or halt the feet. Formed from 足, with abbreviated 適 indicating the sound. Some explain it as the hesitant movement 蹢躅. Palace Attendant Jia explains: dirt on the feet.

shuowen:1366.text: The hesitant movement 蹢躅. Formed from 足, with 蜀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1367.text: To strike against. Formed from 足, with 卒 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to startle; another: the expression 蒼踤. [The final expression is unexplained.]

shuowen:1368.text: To fall prostrate. Formed from 足, with 厥 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to jump. Also pronounced like 橜.

shuowen:1369.text: To spring or stumble, 蹶. Formed from 足, with 兆 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to leap.

shuowen:1370.text: To move. Formed from 足, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1371.text: 歭䠧: not to advance. Formed from 足, with 屠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1372.text: To jump. Formed from 足, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1373.text: People of Chu call jumping and leaping 蹠. Formed from 足, with 庶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1374.text: To reach forward with the foot to seize something, 趿. Formed from 足, with 荅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1375.text: To jump. Formed from 足, with 䍃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1376.text: To advance the foot and seize something. Formed from 足, with 及 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “趿 is called 擷, to seize.”

shuowen:1377.text: To trample or tread over something while walking. Formed from 足, with 貝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1378.text: To stumble. Formed from 足, with 質 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “It stumbles on its tail.”

shuowen:1379.text: To stumble. Formed from 足, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1380.text: To pass over, leap beyond or traverse. Formed from 足, with 丗 indicating the sound. [Duan proposes reading the received gloss 述 as a corrupted graph 𨒋.]

shuowen:1381.text: To stumble, 跋. Formed from 足, with 眞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1382.text: To stumble, 蹎跋. Formed from 足, with 犮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1383.text: Small steps. Formed from 足, with 𦟝 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “I dare not fail to take small steps.”

shuowen:1384.text: To stumble, 踼. Formed from 足, with 失 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to cross.

shuowen:1385.text: To stumble, 跌踼. Formed from 足, with 昜 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to thrust or rush forward.

shuowen:1386.text: To squat. Formed from 足, with 尊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1387.text: To squat. Formed from 足, with 居 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1388.text: To squat. Formed from 足, with 荂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1389.text: To move one’s feet in a careful, shifting or ceremonially constrained manner. Formed from 足, with 矍 indicating the sound. [The precise movement described by 躩如 remains context-dependent.]

shuowen:1390.text: To fall prostrate. Formed from 足, with 咅 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The men of Jin knocked him down.”

shuowen:1391.text: To walk unevenly. Formed from 足, with 皮 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to push with the foot. Read like 彼.

shuowen:1392.text: To limp. Formed from 足, with abbreviated 寒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1393.text: Feet not straight. Formed from 足, with 扁 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a horse dragging its hind feet. Read like 苹; some say like 徧.

shuowen:1394.text: Flesh of the shank. Another explanation: a bent shank. Formed from 足, with 𢌳 indicating the sound. Read like 逵.

shuowen:1395.text: A foot sprained or twisted in stumbling. Formed from 足, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1396.text: The feet touching the ground directly. Formed from 足, with 先 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1397.text: Feet contracted by cold weather. Formed from 足, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1398.text: Frostbitten feet. Formed from 足, with 囷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1399.text: A cock's spur. Formed from 足, with 巨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1400.text: Dancing shoes. Formed from 足, with 麗 indicating the sound.
